scenarios.title: 入职第一天向团队介绍自己
scenarios.setting: 入职第一天上午的团队周会，视频会议。经理 Elena 请你做个自我介绍，在场的还有后端的 Kwame 和设计师 Sophie。你要简短地讲背景和接下来要做的事，并自然地接住同事的提问和玩笑。

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Elena
turns.en: Before we dive into the agenda — we've got a new face today! I've been bragging about you all week, so no pressure. Want to say a quick hello and tell us a bit about yourself?
turns.zh: 在进入议程之前——今天我们有位新面孔！我已经夸了你一个星期了，所以别有压力。跟大家打个招呼，简单介绍一下自己？

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你跟大家打招呼，说很高兴加入。简单介绍自己：你是有八年经验的全栈工程师，最近一份工作是在一家金融科技公司做支付平台。
turns.en: Hi everyone, great to be here. I'm a full-stack engineer with eight years of experience. Most recently, I worked on the payments platform at a fintech company.

chunks.term: I'm a full-stack engineer with ... years of experience.
chunks.zh: 我是一名有……年经验的全栈工程师。

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Elena
turns.en: And you'll be joining the checkout squad, right? Tell them what you'll be working on.
turns.zh: 你是要加入结算小组，对吧？跟大家说说你要做什么。

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你说对，你会先从结算页的前端性能入手。你的背景偏前端框架和接口设计，但后端的活你也乐意参与。头几个星期你的主要目标是尽快熟悉情况。
turns.en: Right, I'll be starting with frontend performance on checkout. My background is in React and API design, but I'm happy to jump in on backend work too. For the first few weeks, my main goal is to get up to speed.

chunks.zh: 让……尽快熟悉情况、跟上进度

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Kwame
turns.en: Welcome! Kwame, backend on checkout. Quick question — what did you use for the API layer at your last place? We're in the middle of a GraphQL versus REST argument, and I need allies.
turns.zh: 欢迎！我是 Kwame，做结算的后端。问个小问题——你上家公司的接口层用的什么？我们正在吵 GraphQL 还是 REST，我需要盟友。

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你开玩笑说第一天你可不站队。你们以前主要用 REST，后来有几个页面换成了 GraphQL。两种都各有取舍，所以你想先听听这场争论的来龙去脉。
turns.en: Ha, I'm not picking sides on day one. We were mostly REST, and moved a few screens to GraphQL later. There are trade-offs either way, so I'd love to hear the context behind the debate first.

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Sophie
turns.en: Diplomatic. I like it. I'm Sophie, I do design for checkout. So, outside of work — what do you do for fun? We need to know who we're dealing with.
turns.zh: 真会说话，我喜欢。我是 Sophie，负责结算的设计。那工作之外——你平时喜欢干什么？我们得知道来的是个什么样的人。

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你说你经常去徒步，大部分周末都在山里。最近还迷上了手冲咖啡，所以想问问大家，公司附近有没有值得推荐的咖啡店。
turns.en: I do a lot of hiking — I'm out on a trail most weekends. I've also been getting into pour-over coffee lately, so if there's a good café near the office — any recommendations?

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Sophie
turns.en: Oh, you have no idea what you've just started. Kwame has a spreadsheet for his beans. An actual spreadsheet.
turns.zh: 哦，你根本不知道你刚才打开了什么话匣子。Kwame 给他的咖啡豆建了一张表格。真的是一张电子表格。

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Elena
turns.en: Okay, okay, before we lose the whole meeting to coffee. Is there anything you need from us this week to get settled?
turns.zh: 好了好了，别让咖啡把整个会都占了。这周为了安顿下来，你有什么需要我们帮忙的吗？

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你说主要两件事：一是把开发环境搭好，二是想和每个人单独聊半小时，了解大家在做什么。你会直接在大家的日历上约时间，时间不合适的话随时可以挪。
turns.en: Mainly two things: getting my dev environment set up, and half an hour with each of you to learn what you're working on. I'll put some time on your calendars — feel free to move it if it doesn't suit you.

chunks.term: put some time on your calendar
chunks.zh: 在你的日历上约个时间

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Elena
turns.en: Love it. Welcome aboard! And Kwame will bring you coffee tomorrow. He just doesn't know it yet.
turns.zh: 太好了。欢迎加入！还有，明天 Kwame 会给你带咖啡，只是他自己还不知道。

scenarios.title: 请同事带你熟悉代码库和流程
scenarios.setting: 入职第三天。你的入职伙伴 Mateus 留了一小时带你过代码库。项目你已经在本地跑起来了，但服务之间的关系、发布流程和第一个任务该做什么，你都还很模糊。Mateus 语速快，习惯满嘴内部缩写。

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Mateus
turns.en: Hey! So, how are you settling in? You've got the repo running, yeah? Cool. I figured I'd just share my screen and zoom through the main folders. Stop me whenever.
turns.zh: 嗨！怎么样，适应得还行吗？代码库跑起来了，是吧？好。我想着就直接共享屏幕，快速把主要的目录过一遍。随时可以打断我。

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你说适应得不错，只是各种工具还在慢慢习惯；项目已经在本地跑起来了。在进入细节之前，你想请他先从整体上讲讲架构，比如一个请求是怎么从前端走到数据库的。
turns.en: Pretty well, thanks — I'm still getting used to all the tools. And yes, it's running locally. Before we get into the details, could you walk me through the architecture at a high level — say, how a request gets from the frontend to the database?

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Mateus
turns.en: Sure. So the web app hits the BFF, the BFF fans out to orders, pricing and inventory, and anything slow goes through the queue to the workers. Oh, and PCS sits in front of pricing. Easy.
turns.zh: 行。Web 应用请求 BFF，BFF 再分发给订单、定价和库存，慢的操作都走队列交给 worker。哦对，PCS 挡在定价前面。很简单。

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你礼貌地打断他：他刚才说的缩写里有两个你没跟上，请他解释一下分别是什么意思。
turns.en: Sorry to interrupt, but you lost me on two of those. What do you mean by BFF and PCS?

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Mateus
turns.en: Ah, sorry, I do that. BFF is backend-for-frontend — the Node layer that shapes data for the UI. PCS is the price calculation service. Honestly, nobody remembers why it's separate.
turns.zh: 啊，抱歉，我老这样。BFF 是 backend-for-frontend——给界面整理数据的那层 Node 服务。PCS 是价格计算服务。说实话，没人记得它为什么要单独拆出来。

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你表示明白了，并复述一遍确认：前端只和那个中间层打交道，其他服务都由它去调用。接着问：如果你要改结算页上的一个字段，通常要动哪几个地方。
turns.en: Got it. So if I understand correctly, the frontend only ever talks to the BFF, and the BFF calls everything else. If I wanted to change a field on the checkout page, which parts would I usually have to touch?

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Mateus
turns.en: Good question. Usually three: the React component, the BFF resolver, and sometimes the API contract, if the field's new. The contract lives in a separate repo, which trips everyone up.
turns.zh: 问得好。一般是三处：React 组件、BFF 的 resolver，如果是新字段，有时还要改接口契约。契约放在另一个代码库里，这一点人人都会被绊一下。

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你说知道这一点很有用。然后问发布流程是什么样的：代码合并以后是自动上线，还是得有人手动触发。
turns.en: Good to know. And what does the release process look like? Once a PR is merged, does it go out automatically, or does someone have to kick it off?

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Mateus
turns.en: Merges to main go to staging automatically. Prod is a button, twice a day, and whoever's on call presses it. Don't worry, you won't be on call for at least a month.
turns.zh: 合并到主干的会自动发到预发环境。生产环境就是一个按钮，一天两次，谁值班谁按。别担心，至少一个月内不会排你值班。

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你说那你就放心了。最后问他：有没有适合新人的小任务可以让你领来做，好让你把从开发到上线的整个流程完整走一遍。
turns.en: That's a relief. One last thing: is there a good starter task I could pick up? Something small, so I can go through the whole flow from development to production once.

chunks.zh: 适合新人上手的入门任务

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Mateus
turns.en: Yep, I tagged a couple for you. There's one about a wrong currency symbol in the order summary — tiny, but it touches all three layers. Perfect first ticket.
turns.zh: 有，我给你标了几个。有一个是订单摘要里货币符号显示错了——很小，但三层都会碰到。特别适合当第一个任务。

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你说这个听起来正合适，今天下午就开始做，要是卡住了会发消息找他。最后谢谢他花时间带你，你真的很感激。
turns.en: That sounds perfect. I'll get started on it this afternoon and ping you if I get stuck. Thanks for taking the time — I really appreciate it.

scenarios.title: 第一周和经理确认期望
scenarios.setting: 入职第一周的一对一视频通话。经理 Elena 想看看你的适应情况，你想问清第一个月的重点、怎么汇报、卡住了找谁。

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Elena
turns.en: So, how's the first week going? Anything blocking you so far?
turns.zh: 第一周感觉怎么样？到目前为止有什么卡住你的吗？

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你说整体很顺利，环境都配好了。你想确认第一个月的重点：先尽快熟悉代码库，还是直接开始接任务。
turns.en: Pretty smooth so far — my setup is all done. I wanted to check the focus for my first month: should I get up to speed on the codebase first, or start picking up tasks right away?

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Elena
turns.en: A bit of both. Start with the onboarding docs and the checkout codebase. By week three, I'd like you to own a small feature end to end.
turns.zh: 两者都要。先看入职文档和结算的代码库。到第三周，我希望你能端到端地负责一个小功能。

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你问汇报方式：每天站会同步够不够，还是希望你周五额外发一份书面更新。另外你说如果进度有风险，你会提前说。
turns.en: Sounds good. How would you like me to keep you posted — is the daily standup enough, or would you prefer a written update on Fridays? Either way, I'll flag it early if anything slips.

chunks.zh: 提前把（风险、问题）说出来

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Elena
turns.en: Standup plus the Friday note is perfect. And if you're stuck for more than an hour, ping me or Kwame — please don't suffer in silence.
turns.zh: 站会加上周五的简短更新就很好。另外，如果你卡住超过一个小时，就找我或者 Kwame——千万别自己闷着。

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你说记下了。你会养成一个习惯：先查文档，查不到就尽早问，而不是靠猜。
turns.en: Got it. I'll make a point of checking the docs first, and asking early instead of guessing.

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Elena
turns.en: That's the spirit. Your onboarding buddy is Sophie — she'll show you the ropes this week.
turns.zh: 就是这个态度。你的入职伙伴是 Sophie——这周她会带你熟悉各种门道。

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你道谢，并确认这周的计划：先看文档和代码，把疑问写进文档里，有解决不了的就在频道里问 Sophie。
turns.en: Thanks, that helps a lot. I'll work through the docs and the codebase this week, write this up in the doc as I go, and ask Sophie in the channel when I get stuck.

chunks.term: write this up in the doc

scenarios.title: 权限没开通，找 IT 跟进
scenarios.setting: 入职第二天，公司笔记本已经到了，但代码仓库和 VPN 都进不去。你先找 IT 支持说明情况，再在团队频道里请 Kwame 先发你文档链接，别干等着。

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Marco
turns.en: Hi, IT support here. I can see your laptop was delivered yesterday — are you all set?
turns.zh: 你好，这里是 IT 支持。我看你的笔记本昨天已经送到了——都弄好了吗？

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你说笔记本没问题，但仓库和 VPN 都登不上去，看起来你的访问权限还没开通。你问是不是要提一个工单。
turns.en: The laptop is fine, thanks. But I can't get into the repos or the VPN yet — it looks like my access permissions haven't been set up. Should I raise a ticket for this?

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Marco
turns.en: Yes, please raise one under Access Requests and pick New Joiner. It usually takes a day. When was your start date?
turns.zh: 好的，请在“访问申请”下面提一个，类型选“新入职”。一般要一天。你的入职日期是哪天？

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你说入职日期是周一，工单刚刚已经提交了。你提醒一下自己已经被拉进站会了，问能不能加急。
turns.en: My start date was Monday, and I've just submitted the ticket. Just flagging that I'm already on the standup invite — is there any way to speed it up?

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Marco
turns.en: I'll bump the priority. In the meantime, docs and chat use a different account, so your team can already add you there.
turns.zh: 我会把优先级提上去。这段时间文档和聊天工具用的是另一套账号，你的团队现在就可以把你加进去。

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Kwame
turns.en: Hey, heard your access is stuck. Want me to send you the onboarding docs so you're not just waiting around?
turns.zh: 嘿，听说你的权限卡住了。要不要我把入职文档发你，省得你干等？

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你先提醒他 IT 正在加急处理，但仓库权限可能还要一天。然后请他把入职文档和设计文档发你，你等的时候先把讨论串的历史看一遍。
turns.en: Heads up: IT is bumping my ticket, but repo access may take another day. Could you share the onboarding and design docs? I'll catch up on the thread history while I wait.

chunks.zh: 把讨论串的历史补看一遍

turns.speaker: them
turns.name: Kwame
turns.en: Links sent. And if it isn't sorted by tomorrow, tell me — I'll chase IT together with you.
turns.zh: 链接发你了。如果明天还没弄好，告诉我——我陪你一起催 IT。

turns.speaker: me
turns.zh: 你向他道谢，说权限一开通你就先把本地环境跑起来，之后就接得上了，有问题再找他。
turns.en: Thanks a lot. Once the access comes through, I'll get the local setup running and pick it up from there. I'll ping you if I hit anything.
